text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- All newspapers report on the arrival of some 2,000 Italian, French and Spanish soldiers belonging to the eight-nation U.N.-backed force due to protect humanitarian aid distribution.

- U.S. fully backs Albanian government of national reconciliation and does not accept any change in the formula reached on March 9 in cross-party talks, American ambassador Marisa Lino told Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.
- Editorial says President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party (DP) wants rebel committees in the south to disband as a precondition for planned June elections.

- Paper says the DP called into question the existence of a broad-based government by accusing Socialists of intentionally sparking the crisis which hit Albania since pyramid investment schemes collapsed earlier this year.
- Italian magistrate ordered an underwater inspection of the Albanian refugee boat that sank after colliding with an Italian navy ship in February, killing as many as 83 people.
- OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky has returned to Albania to meet Albanian authorities on multi-nation force. He will also visit rebel stronghold Vlore and northern town of Shkoder.
- Fino's government hails Italian-led multinational security force, codenamed "Alba", which arrived on Tuesday.
- Four people injured by stray bullets in southern district of Fier.
- Shkoder, where 32 people have died and 150 were injured, is still ruled by criminal gangs, paper says.
- Paper says a reported 14-percent increase in Albania's 1996 gross domestic product has been vastly exaggerated.
- The Democratic Party said in a statement Vranitzky's mission may be compromised if he goes ahead and meet rebels in the south.
